name: square_congruence_from_smooth_relations

phase_0.boundary_condition: The fixed finite factor base and the target integer N define the closed system where all smoothness checks and parity cancellations occur.

⊢.justification: The uninitialized state before any factorization attempt; the raw number to be split.

⊣.justification: The terminal anchor defining the complete set of allowable prime factors for smoothness.

≻.justification: The forward morphism generating candidate numbers x to test against the factor base.

≺.justification: The reverse morphism rejecting trials that contain primes outside the fixed alphabet.

⋈.justification: Sequential chaining of valid smooth relations into a matrix of parity vectors.

⊙.justification: The identity state where the product of selected relations equals a perfect square on both sides.

∈.justification: Splits the accumulated relations into a productive set (linearly dependent) and a non-productive set (independent).

∋.justification: Rejoins the selected relations to form a single congruence of squares x² ≡ y² (mod N).

⊤.justification: The affirmative state where x ≠ ±y (mod N), yielding a non-trivial factor via gcd(x-y, N).

⊥.justification: The negative state where x ≡ ±y (mod N), yielding no new factor and requiring a retry.

⊞.justification: The paradice state holding both the individual non-square relations and their combined square result simultaneously.

⊡.justification: The permanent, append-only record of the discovered factor pair.

phase_2.split_input: Matrix of parity vectors from smooth trials
phase_2.fuse_result: Congruence of Squares (x² ≡ y² mod N)
phase_2.failure_reason: FSPLIT3 at step 4 dangles — no matching FFUSE3

phase_3.void_description: The target integer N exists but no smooth relations have been found or processed.
phase_3.true_description: A non-trivial factor pair (x, y) has been found such that gcd(x-y, N) > 1 and < N.
phase_3.false_description: The generated congruence is trivial (x ≡ ±y mod N), yielding no factor.
phase_3.both_description: The system holds a set of relations that are individually non-squares but collectively form a square, maintaining the tension between the parts and the whole.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the target integer N to be factored.
Define the fixed factor base (small primes) as the boundary for smoothness.
Generate a trial number x and compute x² mod N.
Branch the trial into two paths: smooth over the factor base or not.
Evaluate the non-smooth path; reject the trial as it contains forbidden primes.
Discard the rejected trial and return to the generation phase.
Evaluate the smooth path; accept the trial as a valid relation.
Append the parity vector of the accepted relation to the accumulation matrix.
Repeat trial generation and accumulation until the matrix has more rows than columns.
Branch the matrix analysis into finding a linear dependency or failing to find one.
Hold the state where individual rows are non-squares but their XOR sum is zero (all even parities).
Multiply the selected relations to form the left-hand side square X².
Multiply the corresponding residues to form the right-hand side square Y².
Recognize the identity X² ≡ Y² (mod N) as the structural closure.
Branch the congruence into a productive split or a trivial identity.
Check if X ≠ ±Y (mod N); if true, compute gcd(X-Y, N) to reveal a factor.
Check if X ≡ ±Y (mod N); if true, the congruence is trivial and yields no factor.
Rejoin the productive and trivial branches to determine the final outcome of the factorization attempt.
Record the discovered factor pair permanently if the result is non-trivial.
Conclude the process with the factorization of N or the need for a larger factor base.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The linear algebra solver over GF(2) that translates parity vectors into a dependency set.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The transfer of smoothness status and parity vectors between the trial generator and the matrix accumulator.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The sparse matrix storing the exponent parities of the factor base for each smooth relation.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The loop that generates trials until the matrix rank condition (rows > columns) is met.
phase_5.alfs_store: The fixed factor base and the target integer N serve as the canonical bootstrap store.

phase_6.cycle_cost: Computational effort to test smoothness and solve the linear system over GF(2).
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: A set of random trials with unknown smoothness properties.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A structured set of relations with guaranteed linear dependence yielding a square congruence.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The process converts random trial entropy into structured algebraic information without loss, as the linear dependence is guaranteed by the pigeonhole principle.
